uses.title: Heavy-chiral threshold Wess–Zumino anomaly match
uses.statement:
Statement

On natural-unit Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, take the trivial $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ bundle, zero $SU(3)$ background, and a smooth compactly supported real nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ with $G=dB$. Let $\alpha,\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. Use the model's source-signed chirality convention $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3=-i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, with positive chirality meaning eigenvalue $+1$. Use the model's Grassmann-odd coefficient algebra and conjugation for both Weyl fields: one smooth compactly supported positive-chirality Weyl field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$, one smooth compactly supported neutral negative-chirality mass partner, and the charge-one scalar $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ in the Yukawa term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where $v>0$, $y\ne0$, and $M_H=|y|v$. Fix the transformations $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$, and use the consistent-anomaly representative with no non-invariant local counterterm. For any fixed integer $n\geq1$, consider a specified $n$-point background-field vertex of $\Gamma_H$ with insertions from components of $B$ and/or $\theta$, and incoming real coordinate covectors $p_j=(p_{j0},p_{j1},p_{j2},p_{j3})\in\mathbb R^{1,3}$ satisfying $\sum_{j=1}^n p_j=0$; set $E=\max_{1\leq j\leq n,\,0\leq\mu\leq3}|p_{j\mu}|$. No on-shell condition is imposed. Require $E/M_H\ll1$ only for the low-energy effective-field-theory interpretation of that vertex. This condition applies to its finite set of external legs, not to the Fourier support of the compactly supported backgrounds, and gives no expansion-remainder bound; the exact local anomaly identity below is independent of it.

Adopt the source-derived consistent-anomaly formula for a positive-chirality Weyl field in representation $R$, written in Bilal's Hermitian convention,

$$\delta_{\epsilon}\Gamma_R=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\operatorname{tr}_R\!\left(\epsilon\,d\left(\mathscr A\wedge d\mathscr A-\frac{i}{2}\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\right)\right).$$

For the selected $U(1)_V$ representation, set $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the positive-chirality field transforms as specified above. Since $R=(\mathbf1,+1)$ is one-dimensional, $\operatorname{tr}_R(1)=1$; since $\mathscr A$ is Abelian, its cubic wedge term vanishes. The massless chiral-triangle calculation gives $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\alpha,B)=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G$. Use $Z_H=\exp(i\Gamma_H)$ and the model data's local field-redefinition relation $\Gamma_H=\mathcal F_M[B+d\theta,M_H]-\Delta_M[B,\theta]$, where $\mathcal F_M$ is invariant and $\Delta_M=\Gamma_R^M[B+d\theta]-\Gamma_R^M[B]$. Thus $\delta_\alpha\Delta_M=-\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}$ and the effective-action contribution $-\Delta_M$ transfers the positive local variation to the Yukawa-massive sector independently of $M_H$, so its local variation is $\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G$. If $\Gamma_L$ is any specified remaining-light-sector functional with infinitesimal variation $\mathcal A_L$, and the low-energy theory retains $\theta$ and is required to match this perturbative background anomaly, then

$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}[B,\theta]=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\theta G\wedge G$$

satisfies $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}=\mathcal A_H$ and hence $\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}})=\mathcal A_L+\mathcal A_H=\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_H)$. Its coefficient has no $M_H^{-1}$ factor. This is an exact local perturbative anomaly identity in the adopted formal model and fixed representative; the low-energy interpretation is restricted to the specified finite-leg vertex above. It asserts no global determinant phase, dynamical-gauge consistency, gravitational contribution, non-Abelian generalization, quantitative EFT remainder, or continuum interacting QFT.

uses.title: Scale independence of compatible EFT matching and running
uses.statement:
Statement

Let $K=[t_i,t_f]$ be a compact interval contained in the common open logarithmic-scale domains of a finite-order high-energy EFT and its lower-energy EFT. Use the realified coefficient coordinates, RG vector fields $\beta_+$ and $\beta_-$, flow maps $\Phi_\pm$, and realified matching map $\widehat M_t$ of the finite-order threshold-matching definition. Assume each beta field is continuous and locally Lipschitz in the coefficient coordinates, locally uniformly in scale, and assume every flow used below exists on $K$. Assume the high-energy trajectory remains in the matching-family domain throughout $K$ and its matched image lies in the low-energy beta-field domain. Assume the matching family is jointly continuously differentiable in scale and coefficient coordinates and RG-compatible throughout these domains. For an initial high-energy realified coefficient vector $x_i$ with $(t_i,x_i)\in\Omega_+$ and any matching scale $s\in K$, define the low-energy vector at the fixed final scale by
$$x_-^{(s)}(t_f):=\Phi_-\!\left(t_f,s\right)\!\left(\widehat M_s\!\left(\Phi_+(s,t_i)x_i\right)\right).$$
Then $x_-^{(s)}(t_f)$ is independent of $s$. Consequently, each selected renormalized low-energy amplitude or Green-function value, evaluated at the same final scale, external states, kinematics, infrared regulator, and operator truncation, is independent of the intermediate matching scale through the retained orders. The matching definition makes that low-energy amplitude agree with its selected high-energy counterpart through those same orders. The same conclusion holds for any finite ordered sequence of thresholds when each matching map satisfies the stated compatibility condition and the required flows exist. Contributions beyond the retained loop order, operator dimension, and mass expansion remain separate theoretical uncertainties; this result assigns them no numerical bounds. This is a conditional deduction from the supplied RG and matching data; it neither calculates beta functions or matching coefficients nor establishes a continuum QFT.

uses.title: The selected SMEFT model is a restricted HEFT branch
uses.statement:
Statement

Let $v>0$, let $J=(-v,\infty)$, and use the linearly transforming complex doublet $H$ with hypercharge $Y=1/2$ and the nonlinear fields $h\in J$, $U\in SU(2)$, with the gauge transformations and mostly-plus Minkowski conventions of the two adopted electroweak models. Here $\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$ is the second Pauli matrix. Put $e_2=(0,1)^T$, $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$, and define
$$\Phi:J\times SU(2)\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\},\qquad \Phi(h,U)=\frac{v+h}{\sqrt2}Ue_2.$$
Then $\Phi$ is a smooth diffeomorphism onto the nonzero-doublet field space. Its inverse is obtained from $\rho=(H^\dagger H)^{1/2}>0$ and $\Sigma(H)=(\widetilde H,H)$ by
$$h=\sqrt2\rho-v,\qquad U=\frac{\Sigma(H)}{\rho}.$$
It is equivariant for $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$: for $g_L\in SU(2)_L$ and $z\in U(1)_Y$, under $H\mapsto g_Lz^3H$ one has $U\mapsto g_LU\operatorname{diag}(z^3,z^{-3})^{-1}$ and $h\mapsto h$. The point $H=0$ is excluded; no value of $U$ is assigned there.

For the finite selected SMEFT interaction consisting of the renormalizable terms and the source-defined Warsaw representatives through canonical dimension six, substitute $H=\Phi(h,U)$ and its conjugate into each representative and expand covariant derivatives by the product rule. In the unnormalized radial variable $x=h/v$, every resulting coefficient function multiplying a fixed finite HEFT derivative/Goldstone monomial is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most six. More precisely, after choosing a finite ordered list of the resulting HEFT monomials and a common dimensionally consistent coefficient normalization, the HEFT coefficient tuple is $f=R c$, where $c$ is the finite selected SMEFT coefficient tuple and $R$ is the finite matrix defined by this substitution. Thus its functions and coefficients obey the polynomial and linear-image correlations of this selected branch; they are not freely specifiable smooth HEFT functions. For example, an independent coefficient function $e^x$ is not in the degree-at-most-six polynomial class on any open interval. These radial functions are analytic in $h/v$ before any further field reparametrization.

The canonical-dimension cutoff and the separately defined HEFT chiral/loop grading remain distinct: the substitution does not identify all HEFT classes through a chosen chiral order with the Warsaw list. The result is a conditional statement about the named finite coefficient representatives and their local field substitution, not a proof that a formal algebraic invariant quotient equals the full physical compact-gauge invariant space. It asserts neither that every HEFT lies on this branch nor that every HEFT point has a weakly coupled ultraviolet completion.

uses.title: Leading Wilsonian Superpotential Match at a Supersymmetric Chiral Threshold
uses.statement:
Statement

Adopt full Axiom of Choice as a sufficient ambient assumption for the action data. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ Wilsonian EFT data in the action definition. Let $\Phi$ be a finite collection of light chiral superfields and let $X$ be one heavy gauge-singlet chiral superfield with canonical physical D-term $[X^\dagger X]_D$. Suppose the derivative-free holomorphic high-energy superpotential is

$$W_+(\Phi,X)=W_L(\Phi)+\frac12 M X^2+XJ(\Phi),$$

where $M>0$ has mass dimension one, $[\Phi_i]=[X]=1$, $W_L$ is a gauge-invariant holomorphic function of mass dimension three, and $J$ is a gauge-singlet holomorphic function of mass dimension two. Both functions are defined on the supplied open light-scalar domain $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, where $n$ counts the light scalar components; their values on even Grassmann-valued fields use their finite Taylor extensions about the scalar bodies in $\mathcal D$. The model identifies the physical heavy threshold mass with this positive coefficient $M$. Let $\Pi_0$ denote the projection in the supplied formal superspace-derivative expansion onto degree zero in $\partial_\mu,D_\alpha,\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$, with each $D$ and $\bar D$ assigned degree $1/2$; this is a formal truncation and gives no numerical remainder bound. Assume the declared tree-level threshold prescription varies the full local action, including any additional real D-term, takes the $\Pi_0$ projection of its chiral Euler equation, and substitutes that stationary solution into $W_+$, at external energies $E_{\mathrm{ext}}\ll M$.

Fix finite operator bases and truncations that retain $W_+$ in the high-energy theory and both $W_L$ and $J^2/(2M)$ in the low-energy theory. Precisely, let $P_-$ be the supplied linear projection from the space of admitted holomorphic light-field functions onto the finite span of retained derivative-free F-term representatives, with their supplied coefficient normalizations; require $P_-W_L=W_L$ and $P_-(J^2/(2M))=J^2/(2M)$. Thus the field-degree, engineering-dimension, and inverse-mass cutoffs discard no term of these two functions. Use the action definition's action-to-scheme identifications with a specified holomorphic coordinate block representing these same F-term coefficients, including suppression-scale factors, in the same unrescaled light fields. Then, in these Wilsonian action coordinates, the holomorphic coefficient component of the declared tree-level threshold prescription is

$$W_-^{(0)}(\Phi)=W_L(\Phi)-\frac{J(\Phi)^2}{2M}.$$

The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, renormalization scale $\mu$, $M$, $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$, and operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ remain distinct inputs; no equality among them is inferred. This result gives the leading derivative-free F-term coordinate only. If a smaller truncation does not satisfy the retention condition, the algebraic substituted superpotential is still the displayed function, but its retained representative is only $P_-(W_L-J^2/(2M))$; a discarded operator has no retained coordinate. The matching definition's equality for selected renormalized amplitudes or Green functions, its common infrared regulator, and its retained truncation must still be checked as supplied matching data. No loop, arbitrary one-particle-irreducible, nonperturbative, or continuum statement follows.

uses.title: Wilsonian Superpotential Nonrenormalization in a Finite Supersymmetric EFT Basis
uses.statement:
Statement

Let the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ Wilsonian effective-action data and finite operator basis be as in the action definition, with formal cutoff $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$. Let $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)$ denote the derivative-free, holomorphic chiral integrand of the Wilsonian action, and define its superpotential part by $W_\lambda(\Phi)=F_\lambda(\Phi,0)$. Fix a finite ordered basis of retained light-field superpotential operators and a scale-independent linear coordinate projection $P_{\mathrm{hol}}$ onto that basis. Use the same unrescaled chiral fields, quotient relations, and operator coordinates at every scale. Assume the selected formal perturbative cutoff prescription has the local nondynamical-spurion extension and local derivative expansion specified in the action data; its local counterterms obey chirality as an identity in the coefficientwise formal background-jet algebra before constant-background evaluation, with independent first anti-chiral jets of each unconstrained real coefficient spurion; its perturbative vertices are one-particle-irreducible; its rigid supersymmetry and BRST/gauge Ward identities hold coefficientwise for every local insertion and their counterterms; and it has no local gauge anomaly.

Assume full Axiom of Choice for the selected finite operator-equivalence data. Then, coefficientwise at every perturbative order,

$$P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_\lambda=P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_{\Lambda_0}.$$

Thus every retained holomorphic superpotential coefficient in the fixed unrescaled field basis is unchanged by the formal Wilsonian cutoff evolution. The separately displayed holomorphic gauge coupling may receive a one-loop correction but no higher-loop correction. The real D-term function and Kähler data may change. This does not constrain arbitrary one-particle-irreducible vertices, coefficients after a scale-dependent field rescaling, nonperturbative corrections, or a continuum interacting quantum field theory.
